items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: So, Frank had then hired Herbert Moran because he liked Herbert Moran playing better than White because Herbert was more jazzy.

ctx.x: He's a tall fella in California. He played with the boy. He played with the boy. He played with the one day at the Bunk once. I heard him with Mason Records. He played with the Honey Drippers. Those records we played with Wade Whaley, Frank Paschley's own job.

So, Frank had then hired Herbert Moran because he liked Herbert Moran playing better than White because Herbert was more jazzy. We had two Trump and she had a big band traveling. So, Frank said, now, we can't hire Tom. I don't want no Thomas Taylor. Thomas Taylor's a little drummer. He's living in Chicago now. He's a drummer with us. So, you come up and play a little drum. That boy would be sick two, three nights. Make that money. So, I remember that. I went out there and the nightclub and I played. They wanted…

That was a sub year, around 1923. So, after we left Devonport, we started booking dances. After our contract was up, we started booking dances, playing theaters all over the state of Oklahoma. We got a booking agent, and we played such theaters like the Rialto in Tulsa. The first real theater I ever played in, and they gave us a nice write-up. It was crazy about the jazz band. And somehow, a lot of disincentions came from the band with the piano player. It caused the band to split up in Bristol, Oklahoma. We…

And we all split up. And Tolles and I, we were just coming back to New Orleans to make that trip with his father to go to Mexico. And we got as far as Shreveport, Louisiana, and by that time, Tolles had been bought a big 57-mile Cadillac. And the car broke down, and he wouldn't leave the car. So, I came home on the train, and I went to see his father. So, his father had difficulty in getting musicians to leave. They was afraid to cross the Gulf on the boat. So, I told him I would leave.
